blocks.text: Setting up your Mac for media planning

Digital media planners often juggle multiple browser tabs. Since Google Sheets is a web app, it can get lost in your Chrome window. You can make it feel like a native Mac app. Open Chrome, go to your sheet, and click the three-dot menu. Look for Cast, Save, and Share. Select Install page as app. This creates a dedicated window for your media plan. It stays separate from your research tabs. This simple change reduces context switching.
Essential Google Sheets shortcuts for Mac

Speed is your best friend when you have hundreds of rows of campaign data. Stop reaching for the mouse for every small task. Use these keyboard shortcuts to keep your hands on the keys. Press ⌘ + / to see every shortcut available in the app. Use ⌘ + ⇧ + H to open the Find and Replace tool. If you need to hide rows or columns quickly, use ⌘ + ⌥ + 9 or ⌘ + ⌥ + 0. These small habits save minutes every hour.

items: Use ⌘ + ⌥ + 9 to hide selected rows instantly.
Press ⌘ + ⌥ + 0 to hide columns that contain old campaign data.
Try ⌥ + / to open the Tool Finder and search for any menu command.
Hold ⌘ + ⇧ + H to clean up your data with Find and Replace.

blocks.text: Media plans can grow massive. With a limit of 20 million cells, you have space, but performance matters. Avoid using too many complex array formulas in one sheet. If your sheet feels slow, check your conditional formatting rules. Remove any that are no longer needed. Keep your raw data on one tab and your summary tables on another. This keeps your file responsive. If you encounter errors, check your ranges first. A broken range is the most common cause of a #REF! error.
If your sheet is lagging, try creating a new tab and copying only the values you need to report on. This reduces the calculation load on your browser.
blocks.title: Keep it light

blocks.text: Lazur sits in your Mac notch, ready to help. You do not need to memorize every menu path. Just hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask. Lazur sees your screen and points to what you need. It can explain what a button does or guide you through a complex task. Use it to keep your focus on the strategy instead of the interface.

One common mistake is hardcoding values in formulas. If your budget changes, you have to find and update every single formula. Instead, use a dedicated cell for your budget figure. Reference that cell in your formulas. This makes your media plan dynamic. Another mistake is mixing data types in one column. Ensure your date column only contains dates. If you have text mixed in, your sorting and filtering will fail. Use the Data > Split text to columns tool if you imported messy data.
How to stay organized with your daily tasks

Your day is full of interruptions. Use a system to track your progress. Some planners use a separate sheet for a to-do list. Others prefer dedicated apps. Whatever you choose, keep it consistent. Use the dictation feature with Lazur to capture ideas quickly. Hold fn and speak your task. It appears at your cursor instantly. This helps you get thoughts out of your head and into your system without breaking your flow.

faq.question: Is there an official Google Sheets app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, there is no official native app. You can create a PWA shortcut in Chrome to make it act like one.

faq.question: How can I see all keyboard shortcuts in Google Sheets?
faq.answer: Press ⌘ + / while inside your spreadsheet to open the full list of shortcuts.

faq.question: What should I do if my Google Sheet is running slowly?
faq.answer: Check for too many complex formulas or excessive conditional formatting. Copying only necessary values to a new tab often helps.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with Google Sheets?
faq.answer: Yes, Lazur works in any app on your Mac. You can use it to ask for help with menus or to dictate text into your cells.
